title: Accounts Assistant
description:
We are currently representing a fantastic client who is actively seeking a diligent and experienced Accounts Assistant to join their established finance department. Our client is looking for a capable professional who can hit the ground running, take ownership of the day-to-day transactional finance duties, and ensure the smooth running of the accounts function.

If you have a solid background in finance and are looking for a stable, fast-paced role within a supportive and growing business, this is an excellent opportunity to make a valued impact.

Key Responsibilities
- Ledger Management: Take full ownership of both the purchase and sales ledgers, ensuring all invoices are processed, coded, and authorized accurately and efficiently.
- Reconciliations: Perform regular and accurate bank, supplier, and credit card statement reconciliations.
- Credit Control: Proactively monitor debtor balances, chase outstanding payments via phone and email, and resolve any invoicing disputes.
- Payment Runs: Prepare weekly or bi-weekly supplier payment runs for management approval.
- Month-End Support: Assist the wider finance team with month-end preparations, including journal postings, accruals, and prepayments.
- Expenses: Process employee expense claims in line with company policy.

What Our Client is Looking For
- Proven, hands-on experience working as an Accounts Assistant or in a similar transactional finance role.
- AAT qualification (Level 3 or 4) is highly advantageous, though qualified by experience (QBE) candidates will be strongly considered.
- Strong IT proficiency, particularly in Microsoft Excel (e.g., VLOOKUPs, Pivot Tables) and previous experience using accounting software (e.g., Xero, Sage, QuickBooks).
- High level of numeracy and exceptional attention to detail.
- Excellent communication skills and the confidence to liaise effectively with both internal stakeholders and external suppliers/clients.

title: Administration Assistant
salary_text: £25000 - £30000 per year (Dep on experience + Company Pension)
description:
About Setec

Setec Ltd is an established specialist training provider delivering Rail, Electrical and Health & Safety training. Since being established in 2012, the company has grown rapidly by focusing on client needs, quality and learner-centred training. Setec s experienced learning and development team provides practical training solutions to industry, with a strong focus on sectors where safety is paramount, including rail, transport, utilities and general industry.

The company delivers training at its own sites, at client locations and in field environments, using professionally qualified trainers with specialist technical expertise. Setec places the learner at the centre of its approach and aims to provide training that is engaging, informative, practical and aligned to customer requirements.

How to Apply

To be considered for this position, applicants must submit both an up-to-date CV and a supporting cover letter.

Role Overview

The Administration Assistant will provide reliable and accurate administrative support to the Business Support Manager and wider team within Setec s specialist training environment. The role is focused on supporting the smooth preparation, production, recording and reconciliation of training course materials, alongside general administration and data entry duties.

The successful candidate will be organised, detail-focused and comfortable working to deadlines in a busy office environment. They will help ensure that course packs and supporting documentation are prepared accurately, checked thoroughly and ready for Director approval where required.

Reporting Line

The Administration Assistant will report to the Business Support Manager and will work closely with colleagues involved in training delivery, course administration and operational support.

Key Responsibilities
- Provide day-to-day administrative support to the Business Support Manager.
- Print, collate and produce course materials and course packs in preparation for scheduled training courses.
- Ensure course packs are complete, accurate, well presented and ready within agreed timescales.
- Reconcile completed course packs and supporting documentation prior to Director review and approval.
- Carry out accurate data entry using internal systems, spreadsheets and databases.
- Maintain electronic and paper-based records in an organised and accessible manner.
- Support the tracking of course documentation, approvals and related administration.
- Assist with general office administration, including filing, scanning, photocopying and document management.
- Respond to internal queries professionally and escalate issues where appropriate.
- Maintain confidentiality when handling company, client, learner or staff information.
- Work collaboratively with colleagues to ensure training administration processes run efficiently.
- Carry out other reasonable administrative duties as required by the Business Support Manager.

Required Skills and Attributes
- Strong attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.
- Good organisational skills with the ability to prioritise routine tasks.
- Confident IT skills, including Microsoft Office applications such as Word, Excel and Outlook.
- Good written and verbal communication skills.
- Ability to follow established processes and work to agreed deadlines.
- Reliable, professional and able to maintain confidentiality.
- Positive attitude with a willingness to support colleagues and learn new systems.
- Ability to work independently on routine tasks while asking for guidance when needed.

Experience and Qualifications
- Previous experience in an administration, office support or business support role is essential
- Experience of data entry, document production or maintaining records would be advantageous
- Experience within a training, education, compliance or operations environment would be beneficial but is not essential.
- GCSEs or equivalent in English and Maths are desirable.

Working Style

This role would suit someone who enjoys structured administration work, takes pride in producing accurate documents and is comfortable supporting a busy team. The postholder should be dependable, methodical and able to manage repetitive tasks with consistency and care.

Role Requirements
- Based at Sutton Benger, Chippenham.
- Clean current Driving Licence with access to own transportation.
- Commitment to accuracy, confidentiality and timely completion of administration tasks.
- Willingness to support changing business priorities and wider office requirements.

title: Data Administrator
description:
The Opportunity

We are working with a growing business that is looking to appoint a Junior Power BI / Data Administrator to support the effective management, reporting and analysis of business data.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone at the early stages of their data career who has a genuine interest in Power BI, Excel and data analysis, and is looking to develop their technical skills within a supportive environment.

The role will involve maintaining accurate data, producing reports and dashboards, supporting users and helping the wider business make better use of its data.

The Role

Working closely with colleagues across the business, you will be responsible for:
- Maintaining and updating company databases and data records.
- Supporting the creation and maintenance of Power BI reports and dashboards.
- Importing, cleansing and validating data from different sources.
- Producing regular management information and operational reports.
- Using Excel to analyse data and identify trends, discrepancies and opportunities for improvement.
- Ensuring data is accurate, consistent and kept up to date.
- Responding to requests for reports and information from internal stakeholders.
- Supporting the development of new Power BI reporting as the business requirements evolve.
- Investigating data issues and working with colleagues to resolve them.
- Maintaining appropriate documentation around reports, data sources and processes.
- Providing general administrative support around data and reporting activities.

About You

We are looking for someone who is organised, analytical and naturally curious about data.

You do not need to be an experienced Power BI developer. The most important thing is that you have a good understanding of Excel, an interest in data and the enthusiasm to develop your Power BI skills.

You will ideally have:
- Some experience using Microsoft Excel, including formulas and data manipulation.
- An interest in or some exposure to Power BI.
- Good attention to detail and a methodical approach to working with data.
- The ability to identify errors and inconsistencies within information.
- Good organisational and administrative skills.
- The ability to communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical colleagues.
- A willingness to learn new systems and technologies.
- A practical approach to problem solving.

Any experience with Power Query, SQL, databases, data visualisation or other reporting tools would be advantageous, but is not essential.

What is on Offer?

This is a good opportunity to join an established business in a role where you will be able to develop your technical knowledge and gain further experience across Power BI, data analysis and business reporting.

The successful candidate will receive appropriate training and support, with the potential to develop the role as your experience and technical capability grows.

title: Quality Team Coordinator
description:
Overview

The role will provide high-quality administrative, systems, and research support to the Quality Team, enabling consistent quality assurance across the grant-making cycle. The postholder will administer and improve the team's Salesforce processes and data standards, coordinate key workflows and information management, support the Director of Quality, Quality Assurance Specialist and Impact (MEAL) Coordinator with scheduling and documentation, and deliver defined research tasks and short projects (e.g., into quality assurance approaches, MEAL frameworks, tools and best practice) to strengthen the team's work.

Key internal relationships: Director of Quality; Quality Assurance Specialist; Impact (MEAL) Specialist; Regional Directors, Programme Managers and Project Officers; ICPO; Finance; Data/Systems owners.

Key Responsibilities

Salesforce administration and systems support
- Administer the Quality/Projects components of Salesforce (and associated tools), including user support, data standards, fields/picklists, basic configuration tasks within delegated permissions, and documentation of processes.
- Maintain data quality rules and routines (validation, required fields, definitions, and guidance) and run regular data quality checks, working with colleagues to resolve issues.
- Produce and maintain reports/dashboards for the Quality Team (e.g., pipeline status, stage-gate progress, approvals, conditions, timeliness, data completeness, and quality metrics).
- Log, triage, and coordinate Salesforce improvement requests, liaising with system owners/IT and supporting user testing and roll-out of updates.
- Create and maintain user guidance (how-to notes, short training materials) to support consistent use of Salesforce and associated quality workflows

Administrative support to the Quality Director and team coordination
- Support the Quality Assurance and Impact (MEAL) Specialists with planning timetables, collating papers, maintaining decision/action logs, and following up actions with stakeholders.
- Prepare and format documents to agreed standards (templates, document control, version control) and maintain an audit-ready filing system in SharePoint (or equivalent).

Coordinate team processes, including shared calendars, team meetings, process documentation, and communications that help the Quality Team operate consistently.

Research and special projects (Quality assurance, MEAL and learning)
- Undertake defined research tasks to support the Quality Team's priorities (e.g., QA approaches in grant-making, MEAL frameworks and tools, file review methodologies, sampling approaches, learning loops, and good practice in documentation and audit trails).
- Produce short research summaries/briefings with practical recommendations for the Director of Quality and Specialists, including options, pros/cons, and implications for Barnabas processes.
- Support discreet improvement projects (e.g., updating templates/checklists, improving guidance, piloting a new dashboard or QA tool) and track actions to implementation.

Maintain a small library of standards, templates, guidance, and reference materials (including MEAL and QA resources) for the team.

Pre-Committee Proposal Scrutiny

Formal review of all project proposals before submission to the projects subcommittee to improve quality by ensuring:

o Proposals are internally consistent;

o Proposed solutions credibly meet the identified needs;

o The response is proportionate and broadly consistent with other Barnabas Aid projects of a similar nature;

o Beneficiary selection is conducted appropriately and can be justified;

o The proposal is strategically aligned, represents good value-for-money and meets all of Barnabas Aid's project policies;

o Relevant harms have been considered and mitigated;

o A proportionate M&E approach is in place;

o Prudent but pragmatic financial arrangements (e.g. split into tranches, use of intermediaries) are adopted and justified.

In conjunction with regional teams, undertake light editing of proposals to improve clarity and correct inconsistencies and typographical errors.

Document checks to ensure all due diligence activities have been conducted before proposal is put to the subcommittee.

Post-Committee Follow-up

Track actions provided by committee to ensure projects fully implement committee decisions (e.g. splitting into tranches, reporting requirements, risk management, etc)

Draft, for regional team's approval, project approval/project rejection letters to partners, including all relevant provisions for management of the grants.

Compliance, confidentiality, and continuous improvement
- Handle sensitive information responsibly, ensuring appropriate confidentiality, data protection, and information security practices are applied.

Support the Quality Team to evidence required checks and maintain consistent records across systems and files, raising risks or gaps as appropriate.

Other duties

The above is not an exhaustive list of duties. From time to time, the employee may be asked or required to carry out other additional tasks, or duties, over and above their usual day to day activities. Employees are expected to work collaboratively across the regional team, including providing flexible support and surge cover as needed.

Person Requirement

Essential

Bible-believing follower of Jesus: Demonstrates a personal commitment to discipleship and growing in faith. In good standing with their Church, actively

participating in its life and community. Committed to affirming and signing Barnabas Aid's Statement of Faith.

Educated to degree-level or equivalent, with strong administrative and systems experience.

Evidence of continuous professional development relevant to administration, data/systems, quality, research, MEAL, or project/grants work

Experience in a busy administrative role, supporting multiple stakeholders, scheduling meetings, and coordinating actions to deadlines.

Experience administering or providing 'super-user' support for a CRM/database (preferably Salesforce), including maintaining data standards and producing reports/dashboards.

Experience with document control and shared filing systems (e.g SharePoint), including version control and maintaining audit-ready records.

Experience undertaking structured research tasks and producing clear summaries/recommendations for non-specialist audiences.

Highly organised with strong attention to detail; able to manage multiple deadlines and stakeholders.

Strong systems aptitude: able to document processes, apply data standards, run checks, and support colleagues to use systems consistently.

Ability to produce clear reports/briefings and summarise research into practical recommendations.

Confident with Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Word, Excel, Teams, SharePoint) and comfortable learning new systems.

Discretion and good judgement when handling confidential/sensitive information.

Desirable

Experience working in the charity, international development, or faith-based sector.

Salesforce administration training/qualification (or equivalent CRM certification).

Training in research methods, MEAL, data analysis, or quality/process improvement

Experience in grants administration, governance support, programme/project support, or compliance-focused roles.

Experience supporting QA, audit, MEAL, or learning processes (e.g., file reviews, indicator tracking, learning events).

Ability to build and maintain Salesforce reports/dashboards and/or familiarity with basic Salesforce admin concepts (profiles/permissions within delegated scope).

Familiarity with MEAL concepts (monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning) and how they support quality and learning in programmes.

Understanding of grants governance, restricted funds, and/or donor intent in a charity setting.

Experience working in a distributed/remote team environment.

Personal Qualities

Service-minded and collaborative; enjoys enabling others to do their work effectively.

Proactive and solutions-focused; comfortable addressing issues, prompting actions and following up with colleagues.

Curious and methodical; able to work independently on research tasks and present findings clearly.

How to Apply

Please apply by submitting your CV and a cover letter demonstrating how your skills and experience make you a good fit for this role and for the mission of Barnabas Aid.

undertaking all associated activities (e.g. booking of venues, refreshments etc)Text ProcessingTo apply a high skill level to the production of all text processing as required by senior managers (e.g. Complex reports, tables, minutes, presentations, leaflets, brochures, statistics etc), including the drafting of routine correspondence in the absence of managers; utilising shorthand skills and copy typing as required.Customer Care -To ensure a professional response service to all callers, including:-Being the point of contact for communications, ensuring the highest level of confidentiality, tact and discretion.Providing advice and guidance on Panel processes and requirements to practitioners, managers and attendees as necessary.Records and Information Systems -To be responsible for all records and information held in relation Adoption Panels, including:-Maintaining a confidential filing system, holding sensitive records, both electronic and paper based, ensuring the security of information/data and complying with policy and procedure.To assist with the maintenance of departmental databases Charms and operate all software systems, ensuring the accurate collection and recording of data and information.To interrogate and produce reports from various systems for senior managers as required.To collate statistical and other management information as requested.General Administrative Duties -To support the Business Services Team to deliver the full range of secretarial and administrative services across the Department, including:-To provide advice/guidance to other administrative staff as necessaryTo carry out specific project work, under the direction of the managerTo undertake routine processes associated with Reviews/Conferences of Children who are In Care and subject to Child Protection ProceduresTo respond flexibly to the needs of the whole service, providing cover across teams/Offices as and when requiredAssist in the development of all systems/procedures operating with the Team/Area

title: Receptionist / Administrator (part-time)
description: We are looking to recruit a motivated and enthusiastic Receptionist / Administrator to join our friendly and supportive team in a busy doctors surgery in Calne, Wiltshire. There are two shift patterns available: A: Tuesday (1:30pm-6:30pm), Wednesday (8:00am-1:00pm), Thursday (8:00am-1:00pm) and Friday (1:30pm-6:30pm) (20 hours per week) B: Tuesday (8:30am-6:30pm), Wednesday (2pm-7:30pm) and Thursday (2pm-7:30pm) (20 hours per week) You will need to deal with people at all levels in a calm and courteous manner, even when under pressure. We are looking for strong team players who enjoy a challenge. If you have excellent people skills, good computer skills and a flexible approach to working, we would love to hear from you. Ensure an effective and efficient reception service is provided to patients and any other visitors to the practice Maintaining and monitoring the practice appointments system Processing personal and telephone requests for appointments, visits and telephone consultations, and ensuring callers are directed to the appropriate healthcare professional Computer data entry/data allocation and collation; processing and recording information in accordance with practice procedures Initiating contact with, and responding to, requests from patients, other team member and associated healthcare agencies and providers Providing clerical assistance to practice staff as required from time to time, including word/data processing, filing, photocopying and scanning Explain practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover and ensure that all new patients are registered onto the computer system promptly and accurately Advise patients of relevant charges for private (non General Medical Services) services, accept payment and issue receipts for same. Scanning hospital and other healthcare professional correspondence Keeping the reception area, notice-boards and leaflet dispensers tidy and free from obstructions and clutter Job responsibilities: Opening up/locking up of practice premises and maintaining security in accordance with practice protocols Enter patient information on to the computer as required Taking messages and passing on information Filing and retrieving paperwork Processing repeat prescriptions in accordance with practice guidelines Undertake any other additional duties appropriate to the post as requested by the Practice Manager. Confidentiality In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. Health and Safety The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety Policy, to include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Reporting potential risks identified. Equality and Diversity The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognizes the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Professional / Personal Development The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work. Quality The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources. Communication: The post-holder should recognize the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognize peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly.

title: Patient Navigator/Receptionist
description: This role is 13 hours per week, working in Marlborough and Pewsey sites. Monday: 16:00 - 19:00 Tuesday: 16:00 - 19:00 Wednesday:16:00 - 20:00 Thursday: 16:00 - 19:00 Friday: OFF Pay is £12.75 initially, rising on successful completion of the 3 month probationary period Benefits of working for KAMP include: 5.4 weeks holiday plus bank holidays Enrolment in the NHS Pension Scheme Monday to Thursday Regular staff socials Free refreshments Discount with local opticians Paid membership of the Bluelight discount scheme Within walking distance of unique high streets Full training Any appointment to the Practice is subject to the practice receiving satisfactory checks from the Disclosure and Barring Service concerning any former criminal convictions. Employment with the Practice is not subject to the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974. The main role of our team of Patient Navigators, formerly called Receptionists is to welcome patients, understand their medical needs and help them to access the most appropriate service. This could be any one of the wide range of KAMP clinicians from physiotherapist to social prescriber to GP, or an external provider such as urgent eyecare service or pharmacist to name but a few. They also provide general support to the Practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone. Patient Navigators also take a leading role in educating patients about how to best use the services on offer to them. We are currently recruiting for a Patient Navigator to work 24 hours in our friendly team to provide an effective and efficient service to all patients and visitors to the practice both in person and via the telephone. Excellent communication skills and accuracy are essential. Experience of working within General Practice and with SystmOne would be desirable. The successful candidate will work across both Marlborough and Pewsey surgeries. Please see Job Description in supporting files for full details of this role, including the Person Specification.

title: Bank GP Receptionist
description: We are looking to recruit a reliable and experienced Bank GP Surgery Receptionist to provide short-term cover within our busy and friendly GP practice. This role is primarily to support the Reception team on Thursdays and Fridays, with shifts available between 8:00am and 6:30pm. Additional shifts may also become available to cover annual leave, sickness absence, and other staffing requirements. Main Duties The successful candidate will be responsible for: Greeting and assisting patients in a professional and courteous manner. Managing incoming and outgoing telephone calls. Booking, amending and cancelling appointments using SystmOne and Anima Processing patient requests and enquiries. Handling prescriptions and clinical correspondence in accordance with practice procedures. Supporting clinicians and the wider practice team with administrative tasks. Maintaining accurate patient records and ensuring confidentiality at all times. Essential Requirements Applicants must have previous GP surgery reception experience and be confident working within a primary care environment. Essential criteria include: Previous experience working as a Receptionist within a GP Practice. Experience using SystmOne. Excellent communication and customer service skills. Ability to work calmly and effectively in a busy environment. Strong organisational skills and attention to detail. Understanding of patient confidentiality and data protection requirements. Ability to work both independently and as part of a team. Hours Primarily Thursdays and Fridays. Shifts available between 08:00 and 18:30. Additional ad hoc shifts may be available depending on practice requirements and staff cover needs.

title: Clinical Administrator
description: Make a Difference Every Day Are you a highly organised and compassionate administrator with excellent customer service skills? Do you enjoy supporting busy teams and making a real difference to people's lives? Prospect Hospice is looking for a Clinical Administrator to join our Clinical Administration Team. This rewarding role provides vital support to our Patient Services teams, helping to ensure patients and families receive exceptional end-of-life care across Swindon, Marlborough and North East Wiltshire. In a recent staff survey, 100% of staff said they would be happy with the standard of care provided if a friend or relative needed treatment, and 98% said the work they do has meaning and purpose. Hours: 15 hours a week - The exact working pattern can be agreed with the successful candidate. However, due to service requirements, availability on Wednesdays and Fridays is essential. Please note w e are not part of the NHS agenda for change As a Clinical Administrator, you will provide comprehensive administrative support across our Patient Services teams. You will play a key role in ensuring our services run efficiently and effectively, supporting clinical colleagues to deliver outstanding care to patients and their families. You will often be the first point of contact for patients, carers and healthcare professionals, requiring a calm, professional and compassionate approach when responding to enquiries and managing sensitive information. This is a varied and rewarding role which combines customer service, administration, clinic coordination and data management. Your work will help ensure patients receive the right support at the right time. Key responsibilities include: Providing administrative support across all Patient Services teams. Managing incoming telephone enquiries from patients, carers and healthcare professionals, ensuring calls are handled with sensitivity and directed appropriately. Processing hospital and community referrals using electronic patient record systems. Supporting the administration and coordination of specialist community clinics. Maintaining accurate patient records, including filing, scanning and archiving documentation. Managing incoming and outgoing correspondence. Producing activity reports, caseload information and other service data. Raising purchase orders and supporting invoice reconciliation. Supporting the booking of agency staff and maintaining rotas when required. Arranging meetings, preparing agendas and taking accurate meeting minutes. Ordering equipment, medical supplies, stationery and uniforms. Supporting service improvement through the development of efficient administrative processes. Ensuring all information is managed securely and in line with GDPR requirements. Interviews will take place on 10th September 2026. About You We're looking for someone who is organised, proactive and committed to delivering excellent customer service, with a genuine desire to support patients,families and colleagues. You will be confident communicating with a wide range of people, able to work under pressure and skilled at managing competing priorities while maintaining attention to detail. Interested? Informal enquiries are welcomed. To find out more about the role, please contact Sam Bennetta, Clinical Administration Team Leader, on 01793 816147 . Why Join Prospect Hospice? At Prospect Hospice, we are proud to be a great place to work and thrive. We value our people and are committed to creating an inclusive, supportive and rewarding workplace where everyone can make a meaningful contribution. We offer a great range of benefits, including: 27 days annual leave plus bank holidays (pro rata), rising with length of service. Membership of the NHS Pension Scheme for eligible existing members. Generous contributory pension scheme for all other staff. Discounts with local retailers, gyms and service providers, including Blue Light Card discounts. A commitment to supporting your professional development. Employee Assistance Programme and wellbeing support. Comprehensive induction, training and development opportunities. Free on-site parking. Please refer to the attached job description for comprehensive information regarding the responsibilities, qualifications, and expectations associated with the position.

title: GP receptionist/administrator
description: Full Time or Part Time receptionist/administrator. Starting Salary meeting national minimum wage. Full time working pattern 5days per week (38hrs) Part time working pattern over 3days per week either Monday - Wednesday or Wednesday - Friday. Hours 8am to 4pm with 30min lunch or 10/10.30am to 6/6.30pm with 30min lunch, this is on a 3 weekly rotation. We are seeking a friendly, organised and motivated GP Receptionist/Administrator to join our busy practice team. This is a key frontfacing role supporting patients, clinicians and the wider practice with a range of administrative and reception duties. Your responsibilities will include: Welcoming and assisting patients at reception Handling telephone and online enquiries Booking appointments and managing patient records Processing prescriptions and carrying out general administrative tasks Supporting the practice team with daytoday operations GCSE English (or equivalent) Experience in a customer service environment or within general practice Strong attention to detail and accuracy Confident grammar and written communication skills Solid IT ability and willingness to learn new systems A professional, calm and compassionate approach The post holder will provide a courteous, efficient and effective reception service to all patients, members of the public, staff and other professionals visiting or contacting the Practice. The post holder will ensure effective and timely communication with all members of the Primary Healthcare Team and will carry out all associated administrative tasks in line with Practice policies, with particular attention to confidentiality at all times. Greet and appropriately mark patients as arrived for their appointments. Answer queries from patients and visitors to the practice at reception desk. Answer telephone calls promptly, dealing with requests from patients, other healthcare professionals and companies contacting the surgery. Recording information onto patient records within our clinical system. Making appointments as required, take messages, answer or redirect queries, and pass on accurate and complete information. File and retrieve paperwork as required. Provide administrative support to process repeat prescriptions with the pharmacy team. Input, allocate and scan data accurately onto clinical systems. Initiate contact with patients, colleagues and external healthcare agencies as necessary. General Duties Keep the reception area, notice boards and leaflet dispensers tidy and free from obstructions or clutter. Support the smooth running of the practice as part of the wider administrative and reception team. This list is not exhaustive and is intended to reflect the core elements of the role. Primary Care is a continually evolving environment, and the post holder will be expected to adapt to reasonable changes in duties that remain consistent with the job summary. The post holder is expected to promote and support the health, safety and wellbeing of patients, staff and visitors as outlined in the Practice Health and Safety Policy. They must: Report any incidents, concerns or unsafe practices immediately. Ensure that their own actions do not put others at risk. In carrying out their duties, the post holder will have access to confidential information relating to patients, staff and the business of the Practice. All such information must be treated as strictly confidential. Confidential information must only be shared with authorised personnel involved in patient care or practice operations. Any breach of patient confidentiality may result in disciplinary action, including dismissal.
